findings.finding: `urllib.error.HTTPError.__init__` requires five positional arguments `(url, code, msg, hdrs, fp)`, but the plan only accounts for `code` (from `JIRAError.status_code`). It never specifies what values to supply for `url`, `msg`, `hdrs`, and `fp` when constructing `BackendHTTPError` from a caught `JIRAError`. The `msg` argument becomes `.reason`, which the EXISTING handler at `dispatch_apply_phases.py:127` logs via `exc.reason` — so a wrong or empty value produces misleading diagnostics. The `hdrs` argument is typed as `http.client.HTTPMessage | None`; passing an incorrect type may surface as a runtime `AttributeError` on `.hdrs` access. These are real constructor-signature constraints, confirmed by the test fixtures in this repo (`test_outbound_differ_bound_but_absent.py:104`: `HTTPError(url='http://x/issue/X', code=code, msg='err', hdrs=None, fp=None)`).

A DC reconcile pass tries to set reporter via _update_one_apply_reporter: AttributeError fires on client.set_reporter(), escapes the except urllib.error.HTTPError handler, and fails the update rather than degrading softly — identical to the pre-fix behavior
findings.suggested_fix: Add `get_issue_by_rest` (translates to self._client.issue() + raises BackendHTTPError for JIRAError) and `set_reporter` (translates to the DC user/reporter REST endpoint) to JiraDataCenterTransport's scope in this story, OR add them as stubs that immediately raise BackendHTTPError(code=501) so the existing catch clauses degrade gracefully. Either way, the scope section must list these methods explicitly.

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)
